proofs.proof_tex:
For \(x\in\mathcal X\), define
\[
 Z_x(\theta)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal A}b_r(x)\exp\{\theta^\top q_r(x)\}.
\]
Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:benchmark-normalized}\) gives \(Z_X(0)=1\) almost surely.  Therefore Definition \(\textnormal{def:softmax-rule}\) yields, for every \(a\in\mathcal A\),
\[
 \pi_0(a\mid X)=\frac{b_a(X)}{\sum_{r\in\mathcal A}b_r(X)}=b_a(X)
 \quad\text{almost surely}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Fix \(\theta\in\Theta\) and abbreviate \(p_a=\pi_\theta(a\mid X)\).  The softmax formula and Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:benchmark-positive}\) make \(p_a\) and \(b_a(X)\) strictly positive, and both vectors sum to one by the denominator in the softmax rule and benchmark normalization.  Since \(\log u\leq u-1\) for \(u>0\), application with \(u=b_a(X)/p_a\) gives
\[
 \sum_{a\in\mathcal A}p_a\log\frac{p_a}{b_a(X)}
 \geq \sum_{a\in\mathcal A}p_a\left(1-\frac{b_a(X)}{p_a}\right)
 =1-1=0.                                                        \tag{2}
\]
Taking \(P_X\)-expectations proves \(K(\theta)\geq0\).  Equation (1) also gives \(K(0)=0\).

We next establish the regularity of the optimizer path.  The declared support \(Y\in[-B,B]\) implies \(|m_a(X)|\leq B\) almost surely.  Thus the welfare integrand is bounded in absolute value by \(B\).  The divergence integrand is pointwise continuous in \(\theta\), and, using \(\log p_a\leq0\) and \(b_a(X)\geq\epsilon_b\), it obeys
\[
 0\leq\sum_a p_a\log\frac{p_a}{b_a(X)}
 \leq\sum_a p_a\log\frac1{b_a(X)}
 \leq\log\frac1{\epsilon_b}.                                  \tag{3}
\]
These bounds justify continuity of the expectations directly: if bounded measurable functions \(f_j\) converge pointwise to \(f\), then, for every \(\delta>0\), the sets
\[
 E_N(\delta)=\bigcup_{j\geq N}\{|f_j-f|>\delta\}
\]
decrease to the empty set and, when \(|f_j|,|f|\leq C\),
\[
 E_P|f_j-f|\leq\delta+2C P\{E_N(\delta)\},\qquad j\geq N.
\]
Countable additivity, followed by \(N\to\infty\) and \(\delta\downarrow0\), proves convergence of the expectations.  Consequently \(W\) and \(K\) are continuous and \((c,\theta)\mapsto M_c(\theta)=W(\theta)-cK(\theta)\) is continuous on \(\mathcal C\times\Theta\).

Let \(c_j\to c\).  Compactness of \(\Theta\) implies that every subsequence of \(\theta_{c_j}\) has a further subsequence converging to some \(\theta_*\in\Theta\).  For every \(\vartheta\in\Theta\), Definition \(\textnormal{def:oracle-path}\) gives
\[
 M_{c_j}(\theta_{c_j})\geq M_{c_j}(\vartheta).
\]
Passing to that further subsequence by the preceding joint continuity gives \(M_c(\theta_*)\geq M_c(\vartheta)\).  Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:unique-optimizer}\) therefore gives \(\theta_*=\theta_c\).  Since every convergent subsequence has the same limit,
\[
 \theta_{c_j}\longrightarrow\theta_c.                           \tag{4}
\]

Fix \(c_0\in\mathcal C\).  Choose \(c_1\in\mathcal C\), distinct from and sufficiently close to \(c_0\).  On a common neighborhood of \(\theta_{c_0}\),
\[
 K(\theta)=\frac{M_{c_0}(\theta)-M_{c_1}(\theta)}{c_1-c_0},
 \qquad
 W(\theta)=M_{c_0}(\theta)+c_0K(\theta).                         \tag{5}
\]
Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:smooth-criterion}\), applied on its fixed neighborhood of the optimizer graph, therefore makes \(W\) and \(K\) three times continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of every \(\theta_c\).  Put
\[
 F(c,\theta)=\nabla_\theta M_c(\theta)
             =\nabla W(\theta)-c\nabla K(\theta).
\]
Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:uniform-interior}\) and optimality give \(F(c,\theta_c)=0\).  Moreover,
\[
 \partial_\theta F(c,\theta_c)
 =\nabla_\theta^2M_c(\theta_c)=-H_c,                               \tag{6}
\]
which is invertible by Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:uniform-curvature}\).

For completeness, local existence and uniqueness of a root path follow without an undeclared theorem.  At \((c_0,\theta_{c_0})\), set \(A_0=\partial_\theta F(c_0,\theta_{c_0})\) and \(T_c(u)=u-A_0^{-1}F(c,u)\).  Continuity of \(\partial_\theta F\) permits a closed ball \(D\) around \(\theta_{c_0}\) and a relative interval \(I\) around \(c_0\) such that
\[
 \sup_{(c,u)\in I\times D}\|I_d-A_0^{-1}\partial_\theta F(c,u)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\frac12
\]
and \(T_c\) maps \(D\) into itself.  The mean-value integral makes \(T_c\) a contraction with factor \(1/2\).  Its iterates from \(\theta_{c_0}\) are Cauchy by a geometric-series bound, converge in the closed ball, and have a unique fixed point.  By (4), \(\theta_c\in D\) for all \(c\) sufficiently close to \(c_0\); hence that fixed point is \(\theta_c\).

For an admissible increment \(t\), subtracting the two root equations, using the exact linearity of \(F\) in \(c\), and applying the mean-value integral in \(\theta\) gives
\[
 0=A_t(\theta_{c+t}-\theta_c)-t\nabla K(\theta_c),
 \qquad
 A_t=\int_0^1\partial_\theta F\bigl(c+t,
 \theta_c+s(\theta_{c+t}-\theta_c)\bigr)\,ds.                   \tag{7}
\]
By (4) and continuity, \(A_t\to-H_c\), so division by \(t\) in (7) yields
\[
 \theta_c'=-H_c^{-1}g_c,
 \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad H_c\theta_c'=-g_c.            \tag{8}
\]
All factors on the right of (8) are continuous in \(c\); matrix inversion is continuous here because every \(H_c\) has smallest eigenvalue at least \(h\).  Thus the path is continuously differentiable, with one-sided derivatives at \(c_{\min}\) and \(c_{\max}\).

The interior first-order condition also gives
\[
 0=\nabla M_c(\theta_c)=a_c-cg_c,
 \qquad a_c=cg_c.                                                \tag{9}
\]
Combining (8), (9), and the chain rule proves
\[
 \frac{d}{dc}K(\theta_c)
 =g_c^\top\theta_c'
 =-g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c\leq0,                                  \tag{10}
\]
and
\[
 \frac{d}{dc}W(\theta_c)
 =a_c^\top\theta_c'
 =c g_c^\top\theta_c'
 =c\frac{d}{dc}K(\theta_c).                                    \tag{11}
\]
The inequality in (10) follows because \(H_c\) is positive definite.

It remains to prove strictness and the dichotomy.  First suppose \(\theta_c\neq0\) at a fixed \(c\), and write \(\theta=\theta_c\).  For each \(x\), define
\[
 \ell_x(t)=\log\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}b_a(x)e^{t\theta^\top q_a(x)},
 \qquad
 k_x(t)=\sum_a\pi_{t\theta}(a\mid x)
             \log\frac{\pi_{t\theta}(a\mid x)}{b_a(x)}.
\]
Finite summation and direct differentiation, using \(\ell_x(0)=0\) from benchmark normalization, give
\[
 k_x(t)=t\ell_x'(t)-\ell_x(t),
 \qquad
 k_x'(t)=t\ell_x''(t)
 =t\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_{t\theta}}
       \{\theta^\top q_A(x)\mid X=x\}.                         \tag{12}
\]
Uniform interiority permits \((1+s)\theta\in\Theta\) for all sufficiently small \(s>0\).  Hence
\[
 r_s(x)=\frac{k_x(1+s)-k_x(1)}s\geq0,
 \qquad
 r_s(x)\longrightarrow
 V(x):=\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\theta}
       \{\theta^\top q_A(x)\mid X=x\}.                         \tag{13}
\]
Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:feature-identification}\), used with the nonzero vector \(\theta\), gives \(P_X\{V>0\}>0\).  Hence there are \(\delta>0\) and a measurable set \(E\) with \(P_X(E)>0\) such that \(V\geq2\delta\) on \(E\).  To justify the expectation limit without invoking an undeclared convergence theorem, fix an arbitrary sequence \(s_j\downarrow0\) and put
\[
 E_N=E\cap\bigcap_{j\geq N}\{r_{s_j}\geq\delta\}.
\]
Pointwise convergence in (13) gives \(E_N\uparrow E\).  For \(j\geq N\),
\[
 E_Pr_{s_j}\geq\delta P_X(E_N).
\]
Differentiability of \(K\) makes the limit of these expectations independent of the chosen sequence, and countable additivity gives \(P_X(E_N)\uparrow P_X(E)\).  Therefore
\[
 \theta^\top g_c
 =\lim_{s\downarrow0}\frac{K((1+s)\theta)-K(\theta)}s
 =\lim_{s\downarrow0}E_Pr_s
 \geq\delta P_X(E)>0.                                            \tag{14}
\]
In particular, \(g_c\neq0\) whenever \(\theta_c\neq0\).

Now let \(Z=\{c\in\mathcal C:\theta_c=0\}\).  It is closed by (4).  If \(c_0\in Z\), then (2), \(K(0)=0\), and uniform interiority show that zero is an interior minimizer of \(K\); hence \(\nabla K(0)=0\).  By (5) and Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:smooth-criterion}\), there are \(L<\infty\), \(r>0\), and a neighborhood of zero on which
\[
 \|\nabla K(u)\|\leq L\|u\|.                                  \tag{15}
\]
Continuity (4) permits a relative interval \(I\) around \(c_0\) on which \(\|\theta_c\|<r\).  Integrating (8), using \(\|H_c^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq h^{-1}\), and applying (15), for \(c\in I\) with \(c\geq c_0\) gives
\[
 \|\theta_c\|
 \leq\frac Lh\int_{c_0}^c\|\theta_s\|\,ds.                  \tag{16}
\]
If \(U(c)=\int_{c_0}^c\|\theta_s\|\,ds\), then \(U(c_0)=0\) and \(U'(c)\leq(L/h)U(c)\).  Therefore
\[
 \frac d{dc}\{e^{-(L/h)(c-c_0)}U(c)\}\leq0.
\]
The expression is nonnegative and starts at zero, so it is identically zero.  Reversing the limits proves the same conclusion to the left of \(c_0\).  Hence \(Z\) is relatively open.  Since \(\mathcal C\) is an interval, a nonempty subset that is both open and closed and contains \(c_0\) must be all of \(\mathcal C\); thus either \(Z=\varnothing\) or \(Z=\mathcal C\).

If \(Z=\mathcal C\), then \((W(\theta_c),K(\theta_c))=(W(0),0)\) for every \(c\), so the frontier is constant.  If \(Z=\varnothing\), (14) gives \(g_c\neq0\) for every \(c\), and positive definiteness in (10) strengthens that display to
\[
 \frac d{dc}K(\theta_c)=-g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c<0
 \quad\text{for every }c\in\mathcal C.                         \tag{17}
\]
Integration of the continuous derivative in (17) makes \(K(\theta_c)\) strictly decreasing.  It is therefore an injective coordinate of the frontier, so distinct penalty values cannot generate the same \((W,K)\) pair.

The argument in fact gives the directive's stronger compact-uniform conclusion.  The maps \(c\mapsto g_c\) and \(c\mapsto H_c\) are continuous by (4)--(6), and inversion is continuous under the curvature floor.  Thus the positive function \(c\mapsto g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c\) in the nonconstant case attains a positive minimum on compact \(\mathcal C\).  Consequently there is \(\kappa_K>0\) such that
\[
 \inf_{c\in\mathcal C}\left|\frac d{dc}K(\theta_c)\right|
 =\inf_{c\in\mathcal C}g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c
 =\kappa_K>0.                                                    \tag{18}
\]

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose the oracle frontier \(\{(W(\theta_c),K(\theta_c)):c\in\mathcal C\}\) is nonconstant.  Then there is a constant \(\kappa_K>0\) such that
\[
 \frac d{dc}K(\theta_c)=-g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c\leq-\kappa_K<0
 \quad\text{for every }c\in\mathcal C.
\]
Put \(K_{\max}=K(\theta_{c_{\min}})\), \(K_{\min}=K(\theta_{c_{\max}})\), and \(\mathcal K=[K_{\min},K_{\max}]\).  Then \(K_{\min}<K_{\max}\), every \(k\in\mathcal K\) has a unique inverse \(c(k)\in\mathcal C\) satisfying \(K(\theta_{c(k)})=k\), and \(c(\cdot)\) is measurable and continuous.  On \((K_{\min},K_{\max})\),
\[
 c'(k)=-\{g_{c(k)}^\top H_{c(k)}^{-1}g_{c(k)}\}^{-1},
 \qquad |c(k)-c(\widetilde k)|\leq\kappa_K^{-1}|k-\widetilde k|
 \quad\text{for all }k,\widetilde k\in\mathcal K.
\]
The endpoint conventions are \(c(K_{\max})=c_{\min}\) and \(c(K_{\min})=c_{\max}\).  The clipped extension to every \(k\in\mathbb R\) is defined by \(c^\dagger(k)=c_{\min}\) for \(k\geq K_{\max}\), \(c^\dagger(k)=c(k)\) for \(K_{\min}<k<K_{\max}\), and \(c^\dagger(k)=c_{\max}\) for \(k\leq K_{\min}\).  In particular, the inverse of any prespecified compact interval contained in \((K_{\min},K_{\max})\) is a compact subset of \((c_{\min},c_{\max})\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By Proposition \(\textnormal{prop:softmax-geometry}\), the path \(c\mapsto\theta_c\) is continuously differentiable, \(\frac d{dc}K(\theta_c)=-g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c\), and the frontier is either constant or has strictly decreasing divergence.  We verify the stronger pointwise and uniform statements rather than inferring them merely from strict monotonicity.

If \(\theta_{c_0}=0\) for some \(c_0\), Proposition \(\textnormal{prop:softmax-geometry}\) gives \(K\geq0\) and \(K(0)=0\).  Uniform interiority makes zero an interior minimizer, hence \(\nabla K(0)=0\).  Smoothness makes \(\nabla K\) locally Lipschitz at zero, while the path equation and uniform curvature give \(\theta_c'=-H_c^{-1}\nabla K(\theta_c)\) and \(\|H_c^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq h^{-1}\).  Exactly as in the integral inequality
\[
 \|\theta_c\|\leq\frac Lh\int_{c_0}^c\|\theta_s\|\,ds
\]
and its reversed-limit counterpart, differentiating the exponentially weighted integral proves \(\theta_c=0\) on a relative neighborhood of \(c_0\).  Continuity makes the zero set closed, so its being also relatively open in the interval \(\mathcal C\) implies that it is empty or all of \(\mathcal C\).  Nonconstancy rules out the latter; therefore \(\theta_c\neq0\) for every \(c\).

For any such \(c\), set \(\theta=\theta_c\).  Direct differentiation of the finite softmax sum gives, with
\[
 \ell_x(t)=\log\sum_a b_a(x)e^{t\theta^\top q_a(x)},
\]
the identity
\[
 \frac d{dt}\left\{t\ell_x'(t)-\ell_x(t)\right\}
 =t\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_{t\theta}}
   \{\theta^\top q_A(x)\mid X=x\}.
\]
Feature identification gives a \(\delta>0\) and an event \(E\) of positive \(P_X\)-probability on which
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\theta}
   \{\theta^\top q_A(X)\mid X\}\geq2\delta.
\]
For any sequence of positive difference-quotient increments decreasing to zero, pointwise convergence lets one increase measurable subsets of \(E\) to \(E\) on which every sufficiently late quotient is at least \(\delta\).  Integrating on those subsets and using countable additivity gives
\[
 \theta^\top g_c\geq\delta P_X(E)>0.
\]
Thus \(g_c\neq0\).  Since \(H_c\) is positive definite, \(g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c>0\) for every \(c\).  Smoothness and continuity of \(\theta_c\) make \(g_c\) and \(H_c\) continuous, and the curvature floor makes inversion continuous.  Compactness of \(\mathcal C\) therefore gives
\[
 \kappa_K:=\min_{c\in\mathcal C}g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c>0,
\]
which proves the uniform derivative assertion.

For \(c<t\), integration gives
\[
 K(\theta_t)-K(\theta_c)
 =-\int_c^t g_s^\top H_s^{-1}g_s\,ds
 \leq-\kappa_K(t-c)<0.                                         \tag{19}
\]
Hence the continuous map \(c\mapsto K(\theta_c)\) takes \(\mathcal C\) bijectively onto \([K_{\min},K_{\max}]\), with the stated reversed endpoint conventions.  Its inverse is continuous: if \(k_j\to k\), compactness gives a convergent subsequence of \(c(k_j)\), and continuity plus injectivity forces every such subsequential limit to equal \(c(k)\).  Continuity implies Borel measurability.  Inequality (19), with \(c=c(k)\) and \(t=c(\widetilde k)\) in the appropriate order, gives the displayed Lipschitz bound.  For interior \(k\), division of
\[
 K(\theta_{c(k+u)})-K(\theta_{c(k)})=u
\]
by \(c(k+u)-c(k)\), followed by \(u\to0\), yields
\[
 c'(k)=\{K'(c(k))\}^{-1}
 =-\{g_{c(k)}^\top H_{c(k)}^{-1}g_{c(k)}\}^{-1}.
\]
The clipped extension is continuous at both endpoints by the endpoint conventions and is therefore measurable.  Finally, the continuous inverse maps a compact interior divergence interval to a compact set; strict endpoint ordering keeps that image inside \((c_{\min},c_{\max})\).

prose_updates.tldr: On the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass of FangRidderXie2026, with \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), every nonconstant maintained frontier has a uniformly regular divergence coordinate: \(\inf_{c\in\mathcal C}|dK(\theta_c)/dc|>0\). On any prespecified compact interior subrange of the attainable divergence range, the unique inverse \(c(k)\) supports the uniform fixed-divergence expansion \(\sqrt n\{\widehat W(\widehat\theta_{\widehat c(k)})-W(\theta_{c(k)})\}=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\{\phi^W_{c(k)}-c(k)\phi^K_{c(k)}\}(O_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). A shared conditional multiplier band is therefore simultaneous in divergence and remains valid after any measurable choice from the plotted regular curve. The optimizer influence cancels from this fixed-divergence contrast. The proved foldwise replacement theorem supplies the same-sample nuisance and optimizer-path approximation needed for the multiplier law; set-valued inversion remains the constant-path or nonregular fallback, and the Hessian quadratic form separately calibrates \(n\)-scaled penalized regret.

project_justification.gap: FangRidderXie2026 proves efficiency and regret limits at a fixed positive preference and illustrates a three-arm commitment-savings frontier, but does not provide a simultaneous band indexed by attained divergence after inspecting the curve. Generic indexed-inference results do not establish the fold-specific learned-influence replacement along the same-sample implicit optimizer path, nor do they supply the softmax-specific uniformly invertible divergence coordinate.
project_justification.niche: On the common finite-action exponential-tilt subclass, feature identification, uniform interiority, smoothness, and curvature imply the exact path identities \(H_c\theta_c'=-g_c\) and \(dK(\theta_c)/dc=-g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c\). Unless the entire path is the benchmark rule, the last quantity is continuous and bounded away from zero on the compact penalty interval. This geometry permits regular inversion from divergence to penalty, while the identity \(a_c=cg_c\) cancels optimizer-estimation noise in welfare evaluated at fixed divergence.
project_justification.fill: For every prespecified compact interval inside the attainable divergence range, the note defines the unique population inverse with explicit reversed endpoint conventions and a measurable sample inverse, proves the uniform influence expansion with score \(\phi^W_{c(k)}-c(k)\phi^K_{c(k)}\), and calibrates its simultaneous band with the same multiplier draws used for the joint path. The foldwise product-bias, shrinking empirical \(L^2\) envelope, global argmax localization, totalized Hessian, covariance replacement, and conditional chaining arguments make the band implementable. Set-valued inversion is retained for a constant path, a failed regularity diagnostic, or a relaxed model admitting tangencies or multiple branches.

prose_updates.related_work: FangRidderXie2026 supplies the broader admissible-rule framework and its three-arm commitment-savings frontier. Its Theorems 1, 2, and 5 give fixed-positive-penalty efficiency, quadratic regret, and efficient doubly robust optimizer limits. This note does not claim their general continuous- or mixed-treatment classes: it works on the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered exponential-tilt/softmax subclass, where the faithful coordinate map is \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The advance is a divergence-indexed, post-selection-valid simultaneous welfare band and joint path inference under explicitly stronger path-uniform conditions. BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 supplies a generic estimated-score multiplier architecture, while this note verifies its difficult foldwise same-sample-path replacement inputs. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML supplies the cross-fitting and product-rate architecture, and ChenFang2019 motivates second-order calibration under first-order degeneracy. Eventwise set inversion follows the logic of RenTelschowSchwartzman2024 but is used here as a fallback rather than the primary construction on a regular nonconstant softmax path.
prose_updates.interpretation: A planner can index the displayed curve by an interpretable divergence budget \(k\), rather than by the penalty \(c\). On every prespecified compact interior divergence range, monotonicity and the uniform slope bound produce one penalty \(c(k)\), and the shared multiplier band covers welfare simultaneously for all such \(k\). Consequently any measurable divergence choice made after viewing the plot inherits the simultaneous guarantee. The fixed-divergence influence \(\phi^W_{c(k)}-c(k)\phi^K_{c(k)}\) has no optimizer-coordinate term: movement of the estimated optimizer changes welfare and divergence in the ratio \(c(k)\), so enforcing the divergence level removes that first-order noise. If the population path is constant, or if a relaxed application permits a tangency or multiple branch, the reported object is instead the full set-valued inverse. The separate quadratic process measures penalized-welfare loss at the fitted rule on the natural \(n^{-1}\) scale.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The regular divergence-indexed theorem is restricted to a prespecified compact subset of the interior of \([K(\theta_{c_{\max}}),K(\theta_{c_{\min}})]\); clipping outside the attainable range only totalizes the inverse and is not an endpoint inference claim. The maintained nonconstant softmax model itself has neither a population tangency nor a self-intersection because its divergence derivative is uniformly negative. Set-valued inversion is needed for the constant-path case, for finite-sample diagnostics that do not certify regular inversion, or after relaxing the identification and curvature conditions. Conditional multiplier validity still needs the declared fixed dimension, bounded outcomes and features, overlap, fixed folds, nuisance consistency, product rate, global uniqueness, uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, and positive curvature floor. The totalized Hessian is essential off the high-probability regular event. The results exclude vanishing penalties, weak overlap, growing dimension, adaptive sampling, nonunique optimizers, and claims of optimal tube width; penalized-regret calibration is not an unpenalized-welfare regret theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The contribution is estimation and inference for a causal welfare--divergence frontier on a fixed finite-dimensional, finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass. Identification is taken as given. The headline is the uniform fixed-divergence influence law and its post-selection-valid shared-multiplier band, supported by a proved uniform inverse geometry and foldwise same-sample-path replacement theorem. FangRidderXie2026 covers a broader admissible-rule setting; only the common softmax subclass is compared, using \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The regular inverse result applies on compact interior divergence ranges of a nonconstant maintained path. The constant path and models with tangencies, self-intersections, or failed regularity use set-valued inversion and do not receive the smooth inverse limit. No result is asserted for continuous or mixed treatments, \(c\to0\), weak overlap, growing features, nonunique optima, adaptive samples, or minimax-optimal tube width.

statement_notes.justification: The softmax geometry proves the regularity needed to use divergence, rather than penalty, as the primary plotted coordinate.
statement_notes.gap: FangRidderXie2026 notes that a restricted class need not map preference one-to-one into divergence, but does not give this path derivative, strict softmax dichotomy, or compact-uniform lower slope bound.
statement_notes.consumer: The divergence-indexed welfare theorem uses the uniform slope bound to localize and linearize the unique inverse; users invoke set-valued inversion only in the constant or nonregular fallback.

statement_notes.justification: This lemma records the directive's stronger conclusion: pointwise feature identification and compact path continuity yield a positive uniform derivative bound, a unique measurable population inverse, endpoint conventions, and a Lipschitz inverse on the whole attainable range.
statement_notes.gap: Fixed-preference analysis does not provide a uniformly regular divergence coordinate for simultaneous inference after selecting a point from the frontier.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the deterministic inversion and localization step for the fixed-divergence influence expansion and its compact-interior simultaneous band.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(c\in\mathcal C\).  Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:uniform-interior}\) implies that \(\theta_c\) is an interior point of \(\Theta\), and Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:smooth-criterion}\) makes \(M_c\) differentiable on a neighborhood of that point.  Since \(\theta_c\) is the maximizer specified by Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:unique-optimizer}\), the elementary directional first-order condition applies in every direction in \(\mathbb R^d\):
\[
 0=\nabla_\theta M_c(\theta_c)
  =\nabla_\theta W(\theta_c)-c\nabla_\theta K(\theta_c)
  =a_c-cg_c.
\]
Consequently \(a_c=cg_c\).  By Definition \(\textnormal{def:joint-influence}\), for every \(O\in\mathcal O\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \psi_c^W(O)-c\psi_c^K(O)
 &=\phi_c^W(O)+a_c^\top\psi_c^\theta(O)
   -c\{\phi_c^K(O)+g_c^\top\psi_c^\theta(O)\}\\
 &=\phi_c^W(O)-c\phi_c^K(O)
   +(a_c-cg_c)^\top\psi_c^\theta(O)\\
 &=\phi_c^W(O)-c\phi_c^K(O).
\end{aligned}
\]
This pointwise identity implies the asserted almost-sure identity.  Definition \(\textnormal{def:frx-penalty-map}\) sets \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), so the coefficient in the cancellation is exactly the comparator's optimization penalty; the reporting transformation \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\) does not alter the first-order condition.

We first separate causal identification from estimation.  For every \(a\in\mathcal A\), Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:exchangeability}\), Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:consistency}\), and the support guaranteed by Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:overlap}\) give
\[
 E_P\{Y(a)\mid X\}
 =E_P\{Y(a)\mid A=a,X\}
 =E_P\{Y\mid A=a,X\}=m_a(X).
\]
Thus the already declared identifying functional \(W(\theta)\) equals the causal welfare \(E_P[\sum_a\pi_\theta(a\mid X)Y(a)]\).  Everything below concerns estimation of that identified functional.

Put
\[
 k_\theta(O)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\pi_\theta(a\mid X)
 \log\{\pi_\theta(a\mid X)/b_a(X)\}.
\]
Assumptions \(\textnormal{ass:bounded-outcome}\), \(\textnormal{ass:overlap}\), \(\textnormal{ass:benchmark-positive}\), \(\textnormal{ass:benchmark-normalized}\), and \(\textnormal{ass:bounded-features}\), together with compactness in Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:compact-parameter}\), bound uniformly the functions \(v_\theta\), \(k_\theta\), and their first three parameter derivatives on the neighborhood used below.  Indeed, differentiating the finite-action softmax expresses every such derivative as a finite polynomial in bounded centered features; moreover
\(
 \log\{\pi_\theta(a\mid x)/b_a(x)\}
 =\theta^\top q_a(x)-\log\sum_r b_r(x)e^{\theta^\top q_r(x)}
\)
is uniformly bounded there.  Dominated differentiation is therefore valid.  In particular,
\[
 E_Pv_\theta(O)=W(\theta),\qquad E_Pk_\theta(O)=K(\theta).
\]
By \(\textnormal{lem:penalized-cancellation}\),
\[
 E_PD_c(O)=\nabla W(\theta_c)-c\nabla K(\theta_c)
 =a_c-cg_c=0. \tag{1}
\]

We record explicitly how cross-fitting enters the root-\(n\) calculation.  Conditional on the training complement of fold \(\mathcal I_\ell\), its validation observations remain independent with law \(P\) by Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:iid}\).  For \(u\in\{0,1,2\}\), the conditional mean and \(L^2(P)\)-envelope conclusions of \(\textnormal{thm:foldwise-replacement}\) are
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\left\|E_P\partial_\theta^u
 (\widehat v_\theta^{(-\ell)}-v_\theta)\right\|
 \le C_{\mathrm{sm}}r_{m,n}r_{e,n},
 \qquad
 \|F_{\ell,u}\|_{P,2}\le
 C_{\mathrm{sm}}(r_{m,n}+r_{e,n}). \tag{2}
\]
For completeness, the centered empirical implication used here follows directly from the entropy conclusion of \(\textnormal{lem:softmax-path-entropy}\).  Given the training sample, symmetrization with an independent ghost validation sample, followed by conditioning on the validation points, reduces the expected supremum to a Rademacher sum.  On each finite net, the bound \(E_\varepsilon e^{t\sum_i\varepsilon_i z_i}\le e^{t^2\sum_i z_i^2/2}\), which follows by multiplying \(\cosh(tz_i)\le e^{t^2z_i^2/2}\), bounds the expected maximum by the empirical \(L^2\) radius times \(\sqrt{2\log(2N)}\).  Telescoping over nets of radii \(2^{-j}\|F_{\ell,u}\|_{P,2}\) and using the polynomial covering bound in that lemma yields
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\left\|
 |\mathcal I_\ell|^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_\ell}
 \left[\partial_\theta^u(\widehat v_\theta^{(-\ell)}-v_\theta)(O_i)
 -E_P\partial_\theta^u(\widehat v_\theta^{(-\ell)}-v_\theta)(O)
 \right]\right\|
 =O_{\mathbb P}(r_{m,n}+r_{e,n}). \tag{3}
\]
The entropy integral is finite because
\(
 \sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\sqrt{1+j}<\infty
\).
Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:fold-balance}\) converts fold normalization to \(n^{-1/2}\), and the fixed number \(L\) permits summing (2)--(3) without any independence assertion between training complements.  Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:product-rate}\) then makes the root-\(n\) conditional-mean contribution vanish, while Assumptions \(\textnormal{ass:outcome-estimability}\) and \(\textnormal{ass:propensity-estimability}\) make the centered contribution vanish.  Consequently, uniformly in \(c\),
\[
 \sqrt n\,\nabla\widehat M_c(\theta_c)
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nD_c(O_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1), \tag{4}
\]
and, at derivative order zero,
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat W(\theta_c)-W(\theta_c)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_c^W(O_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1). \tag{5}
\]
Because \(K\) has no estimated nuisance,
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat K(\theta_c)-K(\theta_c)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_c^K(O_i) \tag{6}
\]
exactly.

The uniform localization and uniform first-two-derivative convergence in \(\textnormal{thm:foldwise-replacement}\), together with the distance \(\rho\) in Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:uniform-interior}\), imply that with probability tending to one every \(\widehat\theta_c\) is interior and satisfies the empirical first-order condition.  On that event, Taylor's identity gives
\[
 0=\nabla\widehat M_c(\widehat\theta_c)
 =\nabla\widehat M_c(\theta_c)
  -\overline H_{n,c}(\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c),
\quad
 \overline H_{n,c}=-\int_0^1\nabla^2\widehat M_c
 \{\theta_c+t(\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c)\}\,dt. \tag{7}
\]
Uniform localization, the derivative convergence just cited, and Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:smooth-criterion}\) imply
\(
 \sup_c\|\overline H_{n,c}-H_c\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_{\mathbb P}(1)
\).
Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:uniform-curvature}\) gives \(\sup_c\|H_c^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le h^{-1}\), so (7) is uniformly invertible with probability tending to one.  The bounded Lipschitz one-dimensional class \(\{D_c:c\in\mathcal C\}\) has
\(
 \sup_c\|n^{-1/2}\sum_iD_c(O_i)\|=O_{\mathbb P}(1)
\)
by the same finite-net exponential argument used in (3).  Equations (4) and (7) therefore first give \(\sqrt n\sup_c\|\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c\|=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\), and then the resolvent identity gives
\[
 \sup_{c\in\mathcal C}\left\|
 \sqrt n(\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c)
 -n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nH_c^{-1}D_c(O_i)
 \right\|=o_{\mathbb P}(1). \tag{8}
\]
The summand in (8) is \(\psi_c^\theta\) by Definition \(\textnormal{def:joint-influence}\).

Taylor expansion of \(\widehat W\) and \(\widehat K\) about \(\theta_c\), using (8), uniform gradient convergence from \(\textnormal{thm:foldwise-replacement}\), and uniform continuity of the population derivatives from Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:smooth-criterion}\), yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n\{\widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)-W(\theta_c)\}
 &=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \{\phi_c^W(O_i)+a_c^\top\psi_c^\theta(O_i)\}+o_{\mathbb P}(1),\\
 \sqrt n\{\widehat K(\widehat\theta_c)-K(\theta_c)\}
 &=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \{\phi_c^K(O_i)+g_c^\top\psi_c^\theta(O_i)\}+o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\end{aligned} \tag{9}
\]
uniformly in \(c\).  The quadratic Taylor remainders are
\(
 O_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt n\sup_c\|\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c\|^2)
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1)
\).
By Definition \(\textnormal{def:joint-influence}\), the two summands in (9) are \(\psi_c^W\) and \(\psi_c^K\).  Equations (8)--(9) prove the displayed expansion for \(\widehat\tau\).

For implemented-rule evaluation, apply the mean-value identity to \(\widehat W-W\).  At an intermediate point \(\bar\theta_c\) on the segment from \(\theta_c\) to \(\widehat\theta_c\),
\[
 \sqrt n\left(
 [\widehat W-W](\widehat\theta_c)-[\widehat W-W](\theta_c)
 \right)
 =\sqrt n\{\nabla\widehat W(\bar\theta_c)-\nabla W(\bar\theta_c)\}^\top
 (\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c)=o_{\mathbb P}(1) \tag{10}
\]
uniformly, by uniform derivative convergence and (8).  Combining (10) with (5) proves the implemented-welfare expansion.  Replacing \(W\) by \(K\) and using (6) proves the implemented-divergence expansion.

It remains to establish the asserted process limit.  Continuity and localization of the optimizer path follow from \(\textnormal{thm:foldwise-replacement}\).  Differentiating the interior first-order condition \(\nabla M_c(\theta_c)=0\), justified by Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:smooth-criterion}\) and invertibility from Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:uniform-curvature}\), gives
\[
 H_c\theta_c'=-g_c. \tag{11}
\]
Thus \(\sup_c\|\theta_c'\|<\infty\).  The bounded derivative calculations preceding (1), (11), and \(\|H_c^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le h^{-1}\) imply that for a deterministic finite constant \(C\),
\[
 E_P\Psi_c(O)=0,qquad
 \sup_{c,o}\|\Psi_c(o)\|\le C,qquad
 \|\Psi_c(o)-\Psi_t(o)\|\le C|c-t|. \tag{12}
\]
For finite-dimensional convergence, take any scalar projection \(Z(O)\) of finitely many values of \(\Psi\).  It is centered and bounded by (12).  Its characteristic function satisfies, for fixed \(u\),
\[
 E_Pe^{iuZ/\sqrt n}
 =1-\frac{u^2E_PZ^2}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}),
\]
where the remainder is bounded using \(E_P|Z|^3<\infty\).  Raising this expression to the \(n\)-th power and using scalar projections proves joint Gaussian finite-dimensional convergence, with covariance \(\Gamma\).

For tightness, write \(\mathbb Z_n(c)=n^{-1/2}\sum_i\Psi_c(O_i)\).  For every scalar coordinate, independence in Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:iid}\) and (12) give
\[
 E_P|\mathbb Z_n(c)-\mathbb Z_n(t)|^4
 \le n^{-1}E_P|\Psi_c-\Psi_t|^4
   +3\{E_P|\Psi_c-\Psi_t|^2\}^2
 \le C|c-t|^4. \tag{13}
\]
After an affine rescaling of \(\mathcal C\) to \([0,1]\), consider adjacent points of the dyadic grid of level \(m\).  For any \(0<\gamma<3/4\), the union bound and (13) show that the probability that some adjacent increment exceeds \(\eta2^{-\gamma m}\) is at most
\(
 C\eta^{-4}2^{-(3-4\gamma)m}
\).
Summing over \(m\ge M\), then chaining the binary approximations of two nearby points and using continuity of every finite-sample path, makes the modulus of continuity uniformly small as \(M\to\infty\).  Tightness at one endpoint follows from its bounded second moment.  Since the stack has fixed dimension \(d+4\), this proves tightness in \(C(\mathcal C)^{d+4}\).  The finite-dimensional calculation identifies every subsequential limit with the declared mean-zero Gaussian process \(G\) having kernel \(\Gamma\).  Combining this weak convergence with (8)--(10) proves the full-stack conclusion.

Finally, the frozen cited result \(\textnormal{lem:frx-fixed-efficiency}\) states that, on the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax submodel and at each fixed positive penalty, \(\psi_c^\theta\) is the canonical gradient and its covariance is the efficiency bound.  For deterministic \(c_1,\ldots,c_r\), differentiation along any regular parametric submodel acts coordinatewise, so the canonical gradient of \((\theta_{c_1},\ldots,\theta_{c_r})\) is the stacked vector \((\psi_{c_1}^\theta,\ldots,\psi_{c_r}^\theta)\).  Equation (8) attains its covariance.  Definition \(\textnormal{def:frx-penalty-map}\) gives \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), while the frozen cited result \(\textnormal{lem:frx-fixed-dr-attainment}\) supplies the fixed-penalty efficient doubly robust comparison.  Hence the theorem extends fixed-penalty efficiency uniformly along the stated softmax path and makes no claim about the comparator's broader rule classes.

Define the centered oracle multiplier process
\[
 G_n^\circ(c)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i
 \{\Psi_c(O_i)-\overline\Psi_n(c)\}.
\]
Conditionally on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), this is a centered Gaussian process.  Let
\(
 U_i(c)=\Psi_c(O_i)-\overline\Psi_n(c)
\)
and
\(
 \Gamma_n^\circ(c,t)=n^{-1}\sum_iU_i(c)U_i(t)^\top
\).
The bounds proved in \(\textnormal{thm:uniform-linearization}\) give a deterministic \(C<\infty\) such that
\[
 \sup_{c,o}\|\Psi_c(o)\|\le C,qquad
 \|\Psi_c(o)-\Psi_t(o)\|\le C|c-t|. \tag{14}
\]

We first prove uniform convergence of the oracle covariance without invoking an unrecorded uniform-law theorem.  For each fixed \((c,t)\), Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:iid}\), boundedness in (14), and Chebyshev's inequality give convergence in probability of the empirical means of \(\Psi_c\), \(\Psi_t\), and \(\Psi_c\Psi_t^\top\) to their expectations.  A finite rectangular grid of \(\mathcal C^2\) makes this convergence simultaneous at all grid points.  The Lipschitz bound (14) makes both the empirical and population product maps uniformly Lipschitz, with a deterministic constant independent of \(n\).  Sending the mesh to zero after \(n\to\infty\) therefore gives
\[
 \sup_{c,t\in\mathcal C}
 \|\Gamma_n^\circ(c,t)-\Gamma(c,t)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1). \tag{15}
\]
Here \(E_P\Psi_c=0\), so the population limit is exactly the declared \(\Gamma\).

Conditional finite-dimensional convergence follows immediately from (15), because both the conditional vectors from \(G_n^\circ\) and their limits are centered Gaussian and their covariance matrices converge.  Conditional tightness can also be checked directly.  For every scalar coordinate, (14) gives
\[
 E_\xi\{|G_n^\circ(c)-G_n^\circ(t)|^2\mid O_1^n\}
 =n^{-1}\sum_i|U_i(c)-U_i(t)|^2\le4C^2|c-t|^2. \tag{16}
\]
A centered Gaussian scalar variable of variance \(\sigma^2\) has fourth moment \(3\sigma^4\), as follows by differentiating its moment generating function \(e^{\sigma^2u^2/2}\) four times at zero.  Thus the conditional fourth moment of the increment in (16) is at most \(48C^4|c-t|^4\).  The dyadic union-bound argument in the proof of \(\textnormal{thm:uniform-linearization}\), now applied conditionally, proves asymptotic equicontinuity; the conditional variance at one endpoint is bounded by (14).  Therefore the conditional laws are tight in \(C(\mathcal C)^{d+4}\).

To turn these facts into convergence in probability, take an arbitrary subsequence.  From (15), it has a further subsequence along which the covariance convergence holds almost surely.  Along that further subsequence, conditional finite-dimensional convergence and the preceding conditional tightness show almost-sure weak convergence to the unique Gaussian law with kernel \(\Gamma\), namely the law of \(G\).  This subsequence characterization proves
\[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\{\mathcal L_\xi(G_n^\circ\mid O_1^n),\mathcal L(G)\}
 \longrightarrow_{\mathbb P}0. \tag{17}
\]

By the definition of \(\Delta_i\), using the same multiplier vector in both processes gives the exact coupling identity
\[
 G_n^*(c)-G_n^\circ(c)
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i\Delta_i(c). \tag{18}
\]
The conclusion of \(\textnormal{thm:foldwise-replacement}\), obtained from the entropy bound in \(\textnormal{lem:softmax-path-entropy}\), states that under \(\delta_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\),
\[
 E_\xi\left[\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}
 \left\|n^{-1/2}\sum_i\xi_i\Delta_i(c)\right\|
 \middle|O_1^n\right]=o_{\mathbb P}(1). \tag{19}
\]
If \(f\) is bounded by one and one-Lipschitz for the supremum norm, the coupling (18) gives
\[
 \left|E_\xi f(G_n^*)-E_\xi f(G_n^\circ)\right|
 \le E_\xi\|G_n^*-G_n^\circ\|_\infty=o_{\mathbb P}(1). \tag{20}
\]
The triangle inequality for bounded-Lipschitz distance, (17), and (20) prove the asserted conditional weak convergence of \(G_n^*\).

It remains to verify the implementable covariance.  Since
\(
 \widetilde\Psi_i(c)=U_i(c)+\Delta_i(c)
\), Cauchy--Schwarz and the definition of \(\delta_n\) give, uniformly in \((c,t)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|\widehat\Gamma(c,t)-\Gamma_n^\circ(c,t)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le \delta_n\sup_{u\in\mathcal C}
 \left\{n^{-1}\sum_i\|U_i(u)\|^2\right\}^{1/2}\\
 &\quad+\delta_n\sup_{u\in\mathcal C}
 \left\{n^{-1}\sum_i\|U_i(u)\|^2\right\}^{1/2}
 +\delta_n^2.
\end{aligned} \tag{21}
\]
The supremum in (21) is bounded by \(2C\) using (14).  Hence (21) is \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), and (15) proves
\[
 \sup_{c,t\in\mathcal C}\|\widehat\Gamma(c,t)-\Gamma(c,t)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \longrightarrow_{\mathbb P}0.
\]
Finally, \(\textnormal{lem:ridge-fallback-inactive}\), using Assumption \(\textnormal{ass:uniform-curvature}\), proves \(P(\mathcal E_n)\to1\) and shows that on \(\mathcal E_n\), simultaneously for all \(c\in\mathcal C\), \(\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}}=\widehat H_c\) and their inverses agree.  Definition \(\textnormal{def:multiplier-bootstrap}\) uses this one totalized influence stack for both \(\widehat\Gamma\) and \(G_n^*\), completing every assertion of the theorem.

Define the simultaneous tube event
\[
 \mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{tube}}
 =\left\{(c,W(\theta_c),K(\theta_c))\in\widehat{\mathcal T}_n
          \text{ for every }c\in\mathcal C\right\}.
\]
By \(\textnormal{thm:postselection-tube}\),
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}P(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{tube}})\geq 1-\alpha.
\]
We prove both asserted inclusions deterministically on \(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{tube}}\).  Fix an arbitrary \(k\in\mathbb R\) and an arbitrary \(c\in\mathcal C(k)\).  By the definition of \(\mathcal C(k)\),
\[
 K(\theta_c)=k.
\]
By the divergence-coordinate inequality in the definition of \(\widehat{\mathcal T}_n\), evaluated at this same \(c\),
\[
 \left|\widehat K(\widehat\theta_c)-K(\theta_c)\right|
 \leq \frac{s_K(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)}{\sqrt n}.
\]
Substitution of \(K(\theta_c)=k\) yields
\[
 \left|\widehat K(\widehat\theta_c)-k\right|
 \leq \frac{s_K(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)}{\sqrt n}.
\]
The definition of \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_n(k)\) therefore gives \(c\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_n(k)\).  Since \(c\in\mathcal C(k)\) was arbitrary,
\[
 \mathcal C(k)\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal C}_n(k).
\]

The welfare-coordinate inequality defining the same tube event gives
\[
 \left|\widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)-W(\theta_c)\right|
 \leq \frac{s_W(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)}{\sqrt n},
\]
or equivalently
\[
 W(\theta_c)\in
 \left[
 \widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)-\frac{s_W(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)}{\sqrt n},
 \widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)+\frac{s_W(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)}{\sqrt n}
 \right].
\]
The already established membership \(c\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_n(k)\) shows that this interval is one of the intervals in the union defining \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_n(k)\).  Hence
\[
 W(\theta_c)\in\widehat{\mathcal V}_n(k).
\]
Taking all \(c\in\mathcal C(k)\) proves
\[
 \{W(\theta_c):c\in\mathcal C(k)\}
 \subseteq\widehat{\mathcal V}_n(k).
\]

The choice of \(k\) was arbitrary after fixing the single event \(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{tube}}\).  Consequently both inclusions hold for every \(k\in\mathbb R\) simultaneously on that event; no uncountable intersection of probability events is taken.  If \(\mathcal C(k)=\varnothing\), both inclusions are vacuous.  Otherwise the argument retains every member of \(\mathcal C(k)\), including multiple branches at self-intersections.  It uses only membership and the two tube inequalities, and never uses injectivity, differentiates the path, or divides by \(K'(c)\).  Thus it remains the valid set-valued fallback for constant paths, tangencies, or near-singular inverse problems.  Combining this eventwise conclusion with the displayed probability bound completes the proof.
